subject: Planned maintenance: pinning & bailout plan for Private v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenny Noble <jnoble@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed window and pin/bailout plan for Private v2.4 rollout

Team,

We have a customer-approved upgrade to the Private stack planned for Helix Health: rolling from runtime v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 (includes several runtime optimizations, kernel updates, and a KV cache compatibility fix). Helix asked for a firm maintenance window and a clearly documented fallback plan. Draft below — feedback requested by EOD Mon.

Summary (proposed):
- Window: Thu 2027-06-17 02:00 - 06:00 UTC (Helix confirmed low traffic)
- Version pin: We'll pin production to v2.3.1 via the version-override flag for 48 hours pre-upgrade to ensure reproducible state; guests on dedicated pools will be labeled.
- Canary: 5% of traffic -> v2.4.0 for 20 minutes, then 20% for 1 hour, then full rollout if metrics stable.
- Rollback (bailout): automatic rollback trigger if error-rate > 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes or p50 latency increase > 30%. Fallback uses the pinned v2.3.1 artifact hosted in our internal registry; KV cache draining will be handled with the cache-compatibility shim.
- KMS/key rotation: no KMS rotations during the window. If an emergency rotation is required, ops must escalate to Security (Laura).
- Network changes: none expected. We'll validate firewalls and private peering prewindow.
- DB migrations: none planned — read-only metadata changes only.

Preflight artifacts attached: upgrade-matrix.csv, preflight-checklist.md.

Action items:
- Marcus: provide detailed rollback checklist (commands + time budget)
- Laura: confirm compliance constraints and whether we need additional evidence for Helix before the window
- Evelyn: confirm communications plan and on-call coverage

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Private Operations

1) Audit logging: Helix requires a snapshot of audit logs covering the 7 days prior and the 24 hours post-upgrade. Please ensure we export audit logs and store them in the Helix S3 (temporary grant) or share via secure link.
2) Evidence: They will want the SOC2 regression report for v2.4 kernel changes (attestation). I attached a short evidence-request template to capture the fields they typically want (compliance-evidence-request.docx).
3) KMS: Agreed — no rotations during the window. Add a note to the runbook that key-access tickets will be denied unless signed off by me.
4) Version pinning: ensure the pinning is reversible via API and that the API call is auditable.

Please add the audit export command into the preflight checklist (step 2.b).

Adding technical rollback details and timing estimates. I'm attaching the rollback-checklist.pdf to this thread. High level: 

Pre-upgrade (T-48h to T-1h):
- T-48h: create immutable artifact tag: redwood/private-runtime:v2.3.1-prod-helix-202706
- T-24h: pin traffic via version-override; run smoke tests (suite: smoke_vpc_basic)
- T-2h: snapshot KV caches (read-only), save pointers

Canary phase (T):
- 0-20m: 5% traffic -> v2.4.0, monitor error / latency / mem pressure
- 20m-80m: 20% traffic if stable
- >80m: progressive ramp to 100% if all checks green

Rollback triggers and steps (should be automated where possible):
- Trigger thresholds: error-rate > 1.5x baseline OR p50 latency +30% OR any 5xx spike > 0.5% of requests
- Automated step 1: route canary traffic back to pinned artifact by setting routing-policy back to pinned flag (CLI: redwood route set --pin v2.3.1-prod-helix-202706)
- Automated step 2: if KV incompatibility observed, run cache-drain -> restart shim (script: ops/compat/drain_and_restart.sh)
- Manual step 3: if automated steps fail after 10 minutes, invoke full cluster rollback (documented in rollback-checklist.pdf) — target RTO: 25 minutes from detection to majority traffic back on v2.3.1

Metrics to capture for postmortem: request counts per shard, p50/p95, error classification (model-timeouts vs infra), restart counts.

I'll drop the exact command snippets into Confluence (link below) and add a checkpoint to the preflight checklist for the audit exports Laura requested.

Marcus
